title: Training report 261020
subtitle: Ten calibration, action, reward and curriculum options: audits of every shipped brain, six G1 fine-tunes of the champion that each change one thing (duel_u1 is the unchanged control), the success-gated opponent ladder for Trump and Kim against the G1 league, and two body fixes. Evaluation: eval.py, 3 seeds x 256 duels, Unity leg rule. Charts: TensorBoard, 10-iteration means. Generated by training/scripts/run_report.py.

sections.title: G1: one change per run against the same recipe (options 4-8 and the clip follow-up)

summary.toddler: We tried six new ways to teach the robot to push. None of them beat the robot we already had.
summary.child: Each try changed one thing (how far a joint may move, how actions are squashed, how the ring is rewarded, random tactics, no reward clip). The best one, a per-joint movement range, was only as good as the plain retraining; the others lost most of their duels against the champion.
summary.adult: 400-iteration fine-tunes of careful1 at 2048 worlds with duel_u1's pool and rewards. scale1 (per-joint action scale from careful1's raw p95, folded exactly into the warm start) is level with the control (50/45 vs duel_u1) but loses 35/63 to careful1; mask1 (tanh + torque window) 10/85; pbrs1 (potential instead of ring shaping) 19/80; tactic1 8/85 at Press play; noclip1 29/58. Changing a trained brain's action path or reward shaping costs more than 400 iterations recover.

sections.verdict: No promotion. careful1 stays the G1 champion (the G1 left the game the same evening; its brains stay for the gates). The options remain opt-in for a new body's ladder, where they cost nothing to adopt from the start.

sections.title: Humans against the G1 league with the success-gated opponent ladder (options 9 and 10)

summary.toddler: Kim and Trump practised against easy robots first and harder ones later. They did not get worse this time, but they did not get much better either.
summary.child: The ladder only moved them to a harder opponent once they won half their rounds, and moved them back when they lost too often. Three earlier recipes made them worse than they started; this one kept them about level.
summary.adult: <body>_vs_g1, 400 iterations, opponents weakest first (standing walker, gen1, gen7, careful1), advance at win share 0.5 over 20 iterations, step back below 0.3. Trump: stages 0->1 at 133, ->2 at 173; vs the G1 league 31/49 (fight1 33/59). Kim: 0->1 at 170, back to 0 at 210, ->1 at 250, ->2 at 342; 31/68 (fight1 33/63). Both end on stage 2 of 4.

sections.verdict: The ladder stops the drift below the starting brain that sank every earlier cross-body recipe; it does not yet add strength in 400 iterations. Not shipped: the G1 left the game, and the humans keep fight1.

sections.title: Audits and calibration (options 1, 2, 3, 7)

summary.toddler: We checked how the fighters move, what they see and what they are rewarded for, and fixed two small body problems.
summary.child: The robot brains pushed their joints to the limit a lot; part of the reward was quietly thrown away; Kim's feet overlapped a little and Trump stood slightly crooked. The feet and the stance are fixed, and the fighters play exactly as well as before.
summary.adult: drive_audit: G1 brains on the +-1 clamp 23-42 % of the time while torque-limited 1-4 %; humans about 2 %. reward_audit: the zero clip binds on 18-19 % of fight steps and erases 12-13 % of penalty mass (charts: the clip share logged by the option runs); in the four-way rung opp_radius can pay 32 per round vs a win of 30. obs_audit: Unity duel inputs match training (drift <= 0.27 sd); Kim in the six-way game 20 of 112 inputs off, Trump 8. step_response: hips and waist zeta 0.12-0.22 on every body. Kim's feet 3.6 mm overlap -> 4 mm gap, Trump's hold symmetric; their brains unchanged (Kim fighter vs a standing Kim 98.8 -> 99.0 %, Trump 96.4 -> 97.0 %).
